text:
mae: Heads up: saw tenant A hit severe tail latency when we enabled RDMA offloads. Traces show long waits at pin/grant path before DMA handoff.

owen: any idea if it's PCIe contention or allocator backpressure? :thinking_face:

mae: quick trace: request waits ~90ms in RequestPin -> grant stall before dma_post. PCIe usage was high but not saturated. Looks like our pin semaphore queue is the bottleneck.

li: we have a per-device pin semaphore with max_inflight_pins. When it saturates we block requests; we do FIFO wakeups which can cause head-of-line if a large pin holds for longer.

samir: tradeoffs: (A) keep FIFO for fairness, (B) switch to size-aware scheduling (prefer small pins) to reduce tail latency, (C) allow preemptible pins with revocation to free slots for small, latency-sensitive work.

mae: additional wrinkle: RDMA transfers also need memory registration (rkey) which is expensive and we batch registration to amortize costs — that increases hold time.

owen: proposals:
 - implement size-classed pin lanes: small (<64KB) lane and large lane; small lane gets priority under contention
 - add a per-tenant concurrency cap to avoid noisy neighbors filling pin slots
 - add a revocation protocol: grant token includes revocable flag; if preempted we snapshot minimal state and requeue

li: revocation complexity is high. Generators holding pins might not be safely interruptible mid-kernel. Preempt only for host-backed streaming pins? safer.

samir: alternative: optimistic short-grant: give a provisional grant for short ops (<10ms) without full registration; if transfer needs full RDMA we upgrade to a full pin (may block) — reduces avg latency for many ops.

mae: that optimistic path risks double work if upgrade blocks. But could work for small KV reads where reply fits in small window.

owen: instrumentation: we need histograms for pin_hold_time by size, per-tenant pin_queue_len, and pci_bandwidth_by_tenant. Also trace span around registration and dma_post.

mae: immediate actions:
 - add telemetry + heatmap for pin_hold_time (li)
 - prototype size-class lanes (owen)
 - sketch revocation protocol but gate to host-backed streaming only (samir)
 - add alert: device_pin_queue_len > 50 for 1m -> P2

infra-bot: alert rule created: rdma_pin_queue_saturation (severity: P2) - targets prod/staging. Runbook: /runbooks/rdma-pinning

li: one more: add metadata to grant_token: {lane, revocable, trace_id} to help debugging and reconcilers.

mae: agreed. i'll open a short RFC for lanes + optimistic upgrade. thanks all :thumbsup:
